screening_decisions.reason: This is a review article summarizing various nasal packing materials and their properties. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate steroid-eluting sinus stents.
Retrospective review study design, not an RCT. Does not compare steroid-eluting stents with any control.
Prospective controlled trial comparing revision ESS to primary ESS outcomes. Does not involve steroid-eluting stents as the intervention.
RCT comparing levobupivacaine-soaked PVA sponge packs vs saline-soaked packs. Levobupivacaine is a local anesthetic, not a corticosteroid. Does not meet the intervention criteria.
RCT comparing doxycycline-releasing stents vs placebo stents. Doxycycline is an antibiotic (MMP-9 synthesis suppressor), not a corticosteroid. Does not meet the intervention criteria.

RCT comparing bioabsorbable steroid-eluting implant (mometasone furoate) vs sham procedure in CRSwNP patients. While this is for in-office treatment of recurrent polyposis rather than immediate post-FESS placement, it evaluates steroid-eluting sinus implants in CRS patients who have had prior ESS. Conservative approach to include for further review.
Cross-sectional epidemiological survey studying prevalence of CRS. Not an RCT and does not evaluate interventions.
Review article discussing predisposing factors and pathogenesis of CRS. Not an RCT.

RCT comparing dexamethasone (corticosteroid)-eluting middle-meatal spacer vs placebo (Sinu-Foam alone) in CRSsNP patients undergoing ESS. The spacer functions similarly to a stent by preventing synechiae and delivering steroid locally.
RCT comparing lidocaine-soaked biodegradable foam vs saline-soaked foam. Lidocaine is a local anesthetic, not a corticosteroid. Does not meet the intervention criteria.
RCT comparing hyaluronic acid nasal dressing vs Merocel nonabsorbable packing. Neither intervention releases corticosteroids. Does not meet the intervention criteria.
European position paper/guideline document summarizing evidence and recommendations. Not an RCT.
RCT comparing Merocel middle meatal spacer vs glove-covered Merocel spacer. Neither intervention releases corticosteroids. Does not meet the intervention criteria.
Population-based prevalence report on chronic conditions. Not an RCT and not related to sinus surgery interventions.
RCT comparing bioabsorbable steroid-releasing implants (mometasone furoate) vs non-drug-releasing implants in CRS patients undergoing bilateral ethmoidectomy. Directly matches the protocol criteria.

RCT comparing triamcinolone (corticosteroid)-impregnated bioresorbable dressing vs saline-impregnated dressing in CRS patients with polyposis undergoing bilateral ESS. The dressing functions as a steroid-eluting device similar to a stent.
RCT comparing glove finger-coated PA pack vs PA pack only. Neither intervention releases corticosteroids. Does not meet the intervention criteria.
Prospective review/observational study of surgical failure causes. Not an RCT and does not evaluate steroid-eluting stents.
Review article discussing etiology and pathogenesis of CRS. Not an RCT.

RCT comparing triamcinolone (corticosteroid)-impregnated bioresorbable dressing vs saline-impregnated dressing in CRS patients with nasal polyps undergoing bilateral ESS. Similar to study 16, the dressing functions as a steroid-eluting device.

This is an RCT comparing NasoPore (biodegradable synthetic polyurethane foam) with traditional Merocel spacer. However, neither intervention is a steroid-eluting sinus stent - they are non-steroid nasal packing materials. Does not meet the intervention criterion.
This is a meta-analysis pooling results from 2 prospective RCTs, not an RCT itself. The selection criteria specify inclusion of RCTs only, not systematic reviews or meta-analyses.

This RCT evaluates hylan B gel (elastoviscous gel) as a wound dressing for hemostasis. The intervention is not a steroid-eluting sinus stent - it is a non-steroid gel dressing used for bleeding control.

While this RCT uses triamcinolone (a steroid), the intervention is an absorbable gelatin dressing applied to the olfactory cleft, not a steroid-eluting sinus stent. The device type differs from the specified intervention (stent vs. dressing).
This is a retrospective analysis of 970 endoscopic ethmoidectomies, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the study design criterion.

This is a prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind clinical trial comparing a bioabsorbable steroid-eluting sinus stent with a non-drug-eluting stent in CRS patients undergoing FESS. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, correct population (adult CRS patients undergoing FESS), correct intervention (steroid-eluting sinus stent), and appropriate comparator (non-steroid-eluting stent).

This RCT compares hyaluronan resorbable packing (MeroGel) with standard non-resorbable nasal dressing. Neither intervention is a steroid-eluting sinus stent - they are nasal packing materials without steroid elution.
This appears to be a commentary or review article discussing outcome measures in sinusitis surgery. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate any intervention.

This is a prospective, multicenter, single-cohort trial (case series) without randomization or control group. The selection criteria require RCTs only. Although it evaluates steroid-eluting implants, the study design does not meet inclusion criteria.
This RCT compares hyaluronic acid nasal packs (Merogel) with no packing. The intervention is not a steroid-eluting sinus stent - it is a non-steroid hyaluronic acid packing material.
This RCT compares nonabsorbable packing with saline irrigations. Neither intervention is a steroid-eluting sinus stent - they are conventional nasal packing and irrigation methods.
This is a prevalence survey study using postal questionnaires across European centers. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate any intervention related to sinus stents.

This RCT evaluates triamcinolone-impregnated absorbable nasal dressings. While it contains a steroid, the intervention is a nasal dressing/packing, not a steroid-eluting sinus stent. The device type differs from the specified intervention.

This RCT compares postoperative systemic prednisone versus placebo, but BOTH groups received steroid-eluting spacers. The study does not compare steroid-eluting stents with non-steroid-eluting stents or other comparators - it tests adjunctive systemic steroids in patients already receiving steroid-eluting spacers.
This RCT evaluates topical tranexamic acid (TXA) for reducing bleeding during FESS. The intervention is not a steroid-eluting sinus stent - it is a hemostatic agent applied preoperatively.
This is a review article discussing advantages and disadvantages of various stents used in sinus surgery. It is not an RCT and does not present primary data.

This RCT compares self-cross-linked hyaluronic acid hydrogel with carboxymethylcellulose viscous foam. Neither intervention is a steroid-eluting sinus stent - they are non-steroid hydrogel/foam materials for wound healing.
